name: Familial Schizencephaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Schizencephaly

criteria.description: Presence of unilateral or bilateral clefts lined by gray matter extending from the ependymal surface of the lateral ventricle to the pia mater on brain MRI
Neurological deficits including motor impairment, developmental delay, or seizures consistent with schizencephaly
Positive family history of schizencephaly or related cortical malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic radiological clefts on MRI plus compatible neurological symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not definitive; diagnosis primarily based on imaging and clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cortical clefts lined by heterotopic gray matter
pathognomonic.notes: Identified on MRI as hallmark of schizencephaly
searchTerms: brain grooves filled with misplaced gray matter
abnormal brain folds with extra tissue
cortical clefts with gray matter lining

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital unilateral or bilateral cerebral clefts
searchTerms: birth defect with brain clefts on one or both sides
unilateral or bilateral brain splits present at birth
muscle stiffness and weakness on one side
spastic weakness in one arm or leg
stiffness affecting limbs on one or both sides

common.symptomName: Developmental delay including motor and cognitive impairment

searchTerms: uncontrolled electrical brain activity causing seizures

occasional.symptomName: Cognitive impairment ranging from mild to severe

rare.symptomName: Behavioral abnormalities including autism spectrum features

imaging: MRI demonstrating clefts lined by heterotopic gray matter extending from the lateral ventricle to the pial surface
genetic: Genetic heterogeneity with variable inheritance patterns
other: Clinical neurological examination revealing motor deficits and developmental delay

distinguishingFeatures: Porencephalic cysts lack gray matter lining
Usually acquired postnatally due to vascular insult or infection
Polymicrogyria shows abnormal cortical layering without full-thickness clefts
No CSF-filled clefts extending to ventricles

redFlags: Sudden onset of seizures in infancy
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as vomiting or bulging fontanelle
references: Guerrini R, Dobyns WB. Malformations of cortical development: clinical features and genetic causes. Lancet Neurol. 2014;13(7):710-726.
Barkovich AJ, et al. Pediatric Neuroimaging. 5th ed. 2012.
